jobs.title: Clinical Case Manager
jobs.description:
Job Description:
**Clinical Case Manager**  

**Felton Outpatient Services Solano (FOSS)**  

**Adult Division**  

  

**Agency Overview**  

Felton Institute responds to the needs of our community by providing innovative, evidence\-informed social services that transform lives. Our organization offers 60\+ programs that address mental health, the unhoused, early care and education, those impacted by the justice system, transitional age youth, as well as aging adults. Our programs combine the latest scientific research with cultural sensitivity and a deep commitment to supporting and reflecting on the communities we serve. Felton offers a dynamic, challenging, and supportive work environment where we encourage the use of professional development, that staff can utilize throughout their career.  

  

**Program Description**  

Felton Outpatient Services Solano (FOSS) is a multi\-disciplinary team of clinicians, medical providers, case managers, and administrators that provide recovery\-oriented, culturally responsive, and trauma\-informed manner specialty behavioral health services to clients 18 and older living with a mental health diagnosis, who are Solano residents and/or have Solano County Medi\-Cal or Kaiser Medi\-Cal. The team will assist individuals experiencing moderate to severe mental illnesses that interfere with their ability to live in the community, attend appointments with professionals in clinics and hospitals, and manage mental health symptoms by providing the following outpatient services: assessment, evaluation, plan development, collateral, family engagement, individual therapy, individual rehabilitation, case management, crisis intervention, and medication support.  

  

**Job Description**  

The Clinical Case Manager is licensed or a BBS registered clinician with direct service experience working with individuals experiencing homelessness, substance use, mental health needs, and medical complexity. Referrals for the program caseload come from Solano County Behavioral Health Services and the caseload ranges from 25\-35 clients to provide the intensive services needed. The primary functions include both direct service and interdisciplinary/multi\-agency collaboration. Local travel between agency sites as well as direct service provision to program participants in the office and in the community is expected.  

  

**Specific Responsibilities*** Provides trauma informed, culturally responsive services that include mental health services including modalities ranging harm reduction, contingency management, motivational interviewing, brief solution focused therapy, crisis intervention.
* Elicits and maintains strong working relationships with clients and the care team which may include other professionals, peers, medical providers, and client identified support persons such as chosen family, friends, or others
* Facilitates and tracks linkages, care coordination, and case management among medical and community\- based supports
* Outreaches to shelters, streets, hospitals, and community settings to meet clients where they are at and able to locate clients by use of electronic health record systems and planning with client
* Ensures timely and accurate documentation of all services provided and maintains applicable chart requirements
* Provides inter\-agency collaboration to facilitate problem solving and clinical care
* On\-call consult during working hours to triage clinical emergencies and coordination for coverage to the team
* Serve as a back\-up for the team as needed
* Attend and participate in all assigned trainings for professional, program, and agency development.
* Additional duties as needed.

**Minimum Qualification*** Master’s Degree (or higher) in Social Sciences, Psychology, Counseling Psychology or related field AND current California State Licensure or registered as an associate with the BBS. One year post\-graduate experience in similar setting preferred but not required.
* Two years of experience providing mental health services to individuals with serious mental health challenges, substance use, and homelessness preferred but not required.
* Experience with specific modalities harm reduction, contingency management, substance use disorder treatment, crisis intervention, de\-escalation, and motivational interviewing.
* Charting and documentation experience under insurance payors such as medi\-care, medical, and special population funding.
* Demonstrated proficiency in Microsoft applications, phone based applications, and navigating EHR systems required.
* Strong working knowledge of mental health and substance use disorders with DSM diagnostic skills (clinical interviewing, assessment, structured diagnostic tools where appropriate, and use of available medical records to inform assessment).
* Ability to provide psycho\-education to clients and consultation to community partners to support the client in their recovery process.
* Demonstrated ability to establish trusting, hopeful relationships with clients and community supports with respect of differences of opinion, beliefs, culture, appearances and ways of life.
* Excellent communication (written and verbal) and interpersonal skills.
* Adaptable, open to change, and able to tolerate ambiguity.
* Strong organizational skills, attention to detail, ability to prioritize tasks, and manage time effectively.
* Demonstrated experience as a team player with a welcoming attitude.
* Bilingual applicants encouraged to apply.

**Additional Information:**  

Reports to: Program Director  

Job Type: Full\-time  

Work Schedule: Onsite  

FLSA Status: Exempt
Salary Range: $100,000\-$110,000 Annually (DOE)
Benefits (subject to election and eligibility): Fully\-Paid Medical and Dental Plans; Health Reimbursement Card, Paid Time Off (personal, vacation, and sick time), 403B with company match. **Applying Instruction:**
Candidates should apply for the position at our career page “careers.felton.org” OR directly email

jobs.title: Housing Navigator
jobs.description:
**SUMMARY**:



The Housing Navigator is responsible for diversion, housing\-focused case management, community referrals, housing placement, and linking families with the appropriate destination for continued services.


**ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES**


* Form and foster relationships with housing agencies and permanent housing providers, including supportive housing providers.
* Partner with housing agencies and providers to offer the Member permanent, independent housing options, including supportive housing.
* Connect and assist the Member in getting available permanent housing.
* Coordinate with members in the most easily accessible setting within MCP guidelines (e.g., could be a mobile unit that engages members on the street).
* Conduct or review intake and assessment for family/everyone accessing services to evaluate housing needs, history, and service/support needs. Develop and implement a housing\-focused individual opportunity plan in collaboration with each Member.
* Conduct a tenant screening and housing assessment that identifies the member’s preferences and barriers related to successful tenancy. The assessment may include collecting information on the member’s housing needs, potential housing transition barriers, and identification of housing retention barriers.
* Develop an individualized housing support plan based upon the housing assessment that addresses identified barriers, includes short\- and long\-term measurable goals for each issue, establishes the member’s approach to meeting the goal, and identifies when other providers or services, both reimbursed and not reimbursed by Medi\-Cal, may be required to meet the goal.
* Search for housing and presenting options.
* Assist in securing housing, including the completion of housing applications and securing required documentation (e.g., Social Security card, birth certificate, prior rental history).
* Assist with benefits advocacy, including assistance with obtaining identification and documentation for SSI eligibility and supporting the SSI application process.
* Identify and secure available resources to assist with subsidizing rent (such as HUD’s Housing Choice Voucher Program (Section 8\), or state and local assistance programs) and match available rental subsidy resources to Members.
* Identify and secure resources to cover expenses, such as security deposit, moving costs, adaptive aids, environmental modifications, moving costs, and other one\-time expenses.
* Assist with requests for reasonable accommodation, if necessary.
* Landlord education and engagement
* Ensure that the living environment is safe and ready for move\-in.
* Communicate and advocate on behalf of the Member with landlords.
* Assist in arranging for and supporting the details of the move
* Identify, and coordinate non\-medical transportation to assist Members’ mobility to ensure reasonable accommodations and access to housing options prior to transition and on move in day
* Provide early identification and intervention for behaviors that may jeopardize housing, such as late rental payment, hoarding, substance use, and other lease violations.
* Educate and train on the role, rights, and responsibilities of the tenant and landlord.
* Coach on developing and maintaining key relationships with landlords/property managers with a goal of fostering successful tenancy.
* Coordinate with the landlord and case management provider to address identified issues that could impact housing stability.
* Provide assistance in resolving disputes with landlords and/or neighbors to reduce the risk of eviction or other adverse action, including developing a repayment plan or identifying funding in situations in which the Member owes back rent or payment for damage to the unit.
* Provide advocacy and linkage with community resources to prevent eviction when housing is or may potentially become jeopardized.
* Assist with benefits advocacy, including assistance with obtaining identification and documentation for SSI eligibility and supporting the SSI application process. Such service can be subcontracted out to retain needed specialized skillset.
* Assist with the annual housing recertification process.
* Coordinate with the tenant to review, update and modify their housing support and crisis plan on a regular basis to reflect current needs and address existing or recurring housing retention barriers.
* Continue assistance with lease compliance, including ongoing support with activities related to household management.
* Conduct Health and safety visits, including unit habitability inspections.
* Perform other prevention and early intervention services identified in the crisis plan that are activated when housing is jeopardized (e.g., assisting with reasonable accommodation requests that were not initially required upon move\-in).
* Provide independent living and life skills including assistance with and training on budgeting, including financial literacy and connection to community resources.
* Perform other related duties as assigned.

**QUALIFICATION REQUIREMENTS:**



Paraprofessional or other qualification based on experience and knowledge of the population and processes.


**EDUCATION AND/OR EXPERIENCE:**


* Paraprofessional with at least 2 years of experience or Associates Degree in a social service field, LCSW, or MSW


* Experience working with individuals and/or families experiencing homelessness and case management experience or similar work experience, preferred.

  


**SKILL AND KNOWLEDGE REQUIREMENTS:**


* Ability to work independently and possess strong time management skills. Strong ability to manage time using an online or paper calendar.


* Knowledge and familiarity with harm reduction and motivational interviewing concepts and strategies.


* Previous experience assessing and referring individuals to various community resources, a plus.


* Computer literacy required. Working knowledge of Word, Excel, and Outlook programs. Familiarity w

jobs.title: Homeless Services, Domestic Violence Housing Coordinator (Los Angeles Area or REMOTE ROLE)
jobs.description:
Description

**Homeless Services, Coordinated Entry System Coordinator**
===========================================================

  

ICF’s Homeless Services team works with federal agencies, state and local governments, non\-profits, and other community partners to implement evidence\-based best practices and to innovate and identify new solutions to ending homelessness. ICF is currently seeking an experienced and mission\-oriented candidate to support the management oversight, implementation, and operation of a Coordinated Entry System (CES) for a large Continuum of Care (CoC).


As a critical member of the housing and Coordinated Entry System team, the Domestic Violence Housing Coordinator will manage housing referrals, identify appropriate program openings and unit vacancies, and provide system navigation support to reduce the time between referral and housing placement. The Coordinator will work closely with individuals and families fleeing domestic violence, dating violence, sexual assault, stalking, human trafficking, or other dangerous or life\-threatening conditions to identify barriers, coordinate documentation and applications, support informed housing choices, and facilitate successful transitions to safe and stable housing.


The position serves as a key liaison among victim service providers, housing programs, emergency shelters, Coordinated Entry access points, landlords, legal and advocacy organizations, and other community partners. The Coordinator will ensure that housing coordination activities are trauma\-informed, survivor\-centered, culturally responsive, and conducted in a manner that protects participant safety, privacy, confidentiality, and autonomy.

 ***Please note: This role is contingent upon a contract award. While it is not an immediate opening, we are actively conducting interviews and extending offers in anticipation of the award.***

 **Key Responsibilities:**


**Coordinated Entry Implementation and Housing Coordination**

* Coordinate CES processes and components related to housing identification, matching, referral, application, and placement activities for survivors of domestic violence and related forms of violence.
* Maintain current knowledge of available emergency, transitional, rapid rehousing, permanent supportive housing, affordable housing, rental assistance, and mainstream resources.
* Match eligible households to housing opportunities based on program requirements, survivor preferences (such as self\-identified housing needs, strengths, goals, safety considerations, household composition, and accessibility needs), geographic needs, and available resources.
* Provide housing navigation and application support, including coordination of documentation, landlord communications, eligibility verification, and move\-in activities.
* Monitor referrals and housing applications from initial connection through placement, identifying and addressing delays, barriers, or gaps in coordination.
* Coordinate warm handoffs to appropriate victim services, legal assistance, benefits, behavioral health services, childcare, transportation, and other community resources.
* Work with housing providers to resolve concerns involving eligibility, documentation, referral acceptance, reasonable accommodations, or placement timelines.
* Identify system\- and program\-level barriers that prevent survivors from accessing or sustaining housing and coordinate appropriate resolutions.

 **Safety, Privacy, and Trauma\-Aware Care Provision**

* Integrate survivor\-defined safety considerations into housing searches, referrals, communications, case conferences, and placement activities.
* Maintain secure communication practices and protect personally identifying and location information in accordance with applicable federal, state, local, and organizational requirements.
* Maintain accurate, timely, and appropriately protected records of referrals, housing searches, program openings, placement progress, and service connections.
* Use approved comparable databases to monitor indicators such as referral timeliness, referral acceptance, housing\-search duration, move\-in progress, unsuccessful referral reasons, and housing\-resource utilization.
* Model respectful, trauma\-informed, culturally responsive, and person\-centered communication.
* Immediately elevate potential safety or confidentiality concerns through established supervisory and organizational protocols.
* Ensure that participation in Coordinated Entry does not delay or condition access to emergency shelter, crisis intervention, hotline assistance, or other immediate safety services.

 **Training, Technical Assistance, and Partner Engagement**

* Support quality assurance reviews while ensuring that monitoring and reporting practices do not reveal survivors’ identities or confidential locations.
* Recommend operational changes that improve safety, equitable access, referral efficiency, housing choice, and successful placement outcomes.
* Examine de\-identified or aggregate information to identify disparities, recurring barriers, service gaps, and opportunities for improvement.
* Contribute to the development of operational guides, referral tools, training materials, frequently asked questions, and other resources related to survivor housing coordination.
* Translate housing, Coordinated Entry, confidentiality, and program requirements into clear procedures for service providers and community partners.
* Provide coaching and technical assistance on safe referrals, information sharing, housing matching, and survivor\-centered engagement.

 **Minimum qualifications:**


* Bachelors’ degree in fields related to Human Services, Public Policy and Administration, or Social Work or Welfare, or other clinical or health\-related field; master’s degree preferred; equivalent experience may be considered.
* Minimum two years directly related experience with Continuum of Care program and HUD Coordinated Entry programs.
* Unders

jobs.title: Senior Patient Care Coordinator
jobs.description:
**Newport Beach, California \| Full\-Time**

A growing Newport Beach plastic surgery practice led by a nationally recognized plastic surgeon is seeking an exceptional and highly experienced **Senior Patient Care Coordinator** to join our team.

This is **not an entry\-level administrative position**. We are looking for a proven cosmetic surgery professional who understands the psychology of the aesthetic patient, knows how to build trust and communicate value, and has demonstrated success converting qualified consultations into booked surgical procedures.

The ideal candidate combines exceptional interpersonal skills with strong sales instincts, organization, professionalism, and genuine patient care. You should be comfortable working with discerning cosmetic patients considering high\-value elective procedures and understand that successful aesthetic sales are built through education, responsiveness, trust, follow\-through, and an exceptional patient experience.

The Role

The Senior Patient Care Coordinator serves as one of the primary relationships between our patients and surgeon, guiding prospective patients from their initial inquiry and consultation through surgery and the postoperative experience.

Your primary responsibility will be to **develop strong patient relationships, communicate the value of our surgeons and services, and convert qualified prospective patients into booked surgical procedures while delivering an exceptional level of service.**

Responsibilities include:

* Conduct comprehensive cosmetic surgery consultations and guide patients through their treatment options and surgical journey.
* Clearly communicate procedure recommendations, surgeon qualifications, expected patient experience, fees, financing options, and practice policies.
* Prepare accurate surgical proposals and financial quotes and follow prospective patients through the decision\-making process.
* Build trust, identify patient concerns, navigate objections thoughtfully, and convert qualified consultations into booked procedures.
* Proactively and consistently follow up with new inquiries, consultations, previous leads, and prospective patients through phone, text, email, and CRM systems.
* Reactivate prior inquiries and consultations and identify opportunities for repeat procedures and patient referrals.
* Coordinate surgical scheduling, deposits, financing, preoperative requirements, and communication between patients, surgeons, clinical staff, and surgical facilities.
* Maintain accurate and timely documentation within the practice EMR and CRM.
* Provide outstanding communication and concierge\-level service throughout the preoperative, perioperative, and postoperative experience.
* Collaborate with the practice's marketing team to maximize lead conversion, identify patient acquisition opportunities, support events and internal marketing initiatives, and strengthen patient referrals.
* Maintain strict confidentiality and adherence to HIPAA and all applicable practice policies.

Who We Are Looking For

The successful candidate will have **at least five years of meaningful Patient Care Coordinator experience within cosmetic plastic surgery or a closely related high\-end aesthetic medical environment.**

Strong candidates will demonstrate:

* A proven track record of successfully converting cosmetic consultations into booked procedures.
* Significant experience discussing and closing high\-value elective surgical procedures.
* A sophisticated understanding of the cosmetic patient and the ability to establish trust without relying on high\-pressure sales tactics.
* Exceptional interpersonal and communication skills in person, by phone, text, and email.
* A warm, polished, professional, confident, and highly service\-oriented presence.
* Strong follow\-up discipline and the ability to manage a large pipeline of prospective patients without allowing opportunities to fall through the cracks.
* Excellent organizational skills and meticulous attention to detail.
* Experience with EMR and CRM platforms and confidence learning new technology.
* Strong computer skills, including proficiency with Microsoft Office and modern digital communication platforms.
* Experience with patient financing and financial discussions surrounding elective procedures.
* The ability to work independently, take ownership of results, and identify opportunities to improve patient conversion and the overall patient experience.
* High integrity, discretion, accountability, and respect for patient confidentiality.

Experience with practice growth, internal marketing, social media, events, referral development, or aesthetic practice management is a significant plus.

**Orange County candidates and candidates with established experience in the Southern California cosmetic surgery market are preferred.**

What Success Looks Like

We are looking for someone who views this position as more than scheduling and administration.

A successful coordinator will become a trusted extension of our surgeon and an advocate for our patients. You will understand where every prospective patient is within the decision\-making process, follow up consistently and intelligently, and help patients feel confident and well cared for from their first interaction with the practice.

Performance will be measured not simply by activity, but by **patient experience, responsiveness, consultation conversion, surgical bookings, follow\-up discipline, and contribution to the growth of the practice.**

Compensation \& Schedule

**Full\-time, Monday–Friday, 9:00 AM–5:00 PM**  
Newport Beach, California

Compensation will include a **competitive base salary plus performance\-based incentive compensation**, with significant earning potential for an experienced, high\-performing cosmetic surgery coordinator.

Specific compensation will be based on experience and demonstrated performance.

How to Apply

Please submit:

* Your current resume
* A brief cover letter describing

Job Description:
**Case Manager****The Knox Support Services****Senior Division** **Agency Overview**
Felton Institute responds to the needs of our community by providing innovative, evidence\-informed social services that transform lives. Our organization offers 60\+ programs that address mental health, the unhoused, early care and education, those impacted by the justice system, transitional age youth, as well as aging adults. Our programs combine the latest scientific research with cultural sensitivity and a deep commitment to supporting and reflecting the communities we serve. Felton offers a dynamic, challenging, and supportive work environment where we encourage the use of professional development, that staff can utilize throughout their career. **Program Description**
Felton’s Senior Division specializes in a full continuum of mental health services for older adults in outpatient clinics, the community, and supportive housing sites, as well as programs in employment training, economic security, case management, advocacy, and social connection and inclusion.  

Felton’s Knox Supportive Services Program provides onsite case management, wellness support services, and behavioral health services to assist tenants with a LOSP subsidy at The Knox. Services aim to support tenants in maintaining stable housing and improving access to resources. Supported tenants were formerly unhoused adults with co\-occurring mental health, substance abuse, medical problems, and limited experience living independently. Support services include case management and behavioral health counseling, referral to and coordination with primary medical care, substance abuse and psychiatric treatment referrals, benefits counseling and client advocacy, meal programs, health education, community building, tenant organizing, and all other case management functions. Felton is committed to implementing evidence\-based practices and behavioral health research within its community\-based mental health services. **Job Description**
Under supervision of the Program Director, the case manager participates in a multidisciplinary team, including external and internal agency team members consisting of mental health clinicians, primary care providers, nurses, peer specialists, interns, and psychiatric medication providers. The program serves 30 tenants at The Knox. The tenants occupying the additional units in the building will not be part of the case manager’s caseload. The caseload is capped at a lower level to allow for intensive services to stabilize individuals who experience acute symptoms and related risk factors. The case manager evaluates needs of clients and works in partnership with a mental health clinician and program director to support the client with coordination of care. Services may include crisis intervention, connection to community resources, client advocacy, and engagement strategies. The case manager maintains accurate, detailed records of client contacts and incident reports as required by Felton, HSH, and county and state regulations. Additional duties are assigned as needed. This position requires the ability to perform the essential functions of the role with or without reasonable accommodation. These functions may include moving and positioning items weighing up to 40 pounds, bending, reaching, stooping, moving throughout the work environment as needed, and responding promptly and safely to urgent or emergency situations, including moving quickly to provide assistance when necessary.  

**Specific Responsibilities*** Work closely with interdisciplinary team.
* Communicate effectively with all team members internally and with partnering agencies.
* Perform intakes and service plan development for adults with a history of being unhoused and other psychiatric or medical conditions or disabilities.
* Provide case management services, which could include connection to primary care, coordination with other providers and community resources, housing stabilization services, etc.
* Maintain records of each client contact or service in accordance with mandated standards of HSH and Felton. Meet requirements of timely access for client care and documentation.
* Participate in team meetings and case conferences through presentation of cases, discussion of issues and exchange of information and ideas.
* Provide crisis intervention to prevent hospitalization and collaborate with clinician as needed.
* Respond to emergency situations as they arise.
* Address specific housing needs via training, coaching, or community resource referrals to support clients in maintaining stable housing.
* Commit to ongoing training, including developing specializations in evidence\-based practices.
* Use the ONE system to maintain client records related to housing per HSH standards.
* Deliver exceptional customer service to clients, community partners, and team.
* Other duties and responsibilities as assigned.

**Minimum Qualifications*** A minimum 2 years of case management for at\-risk populations, including co\-occurring disorders.
* Experience working with unhoused or formerly unhoused community members, with a strong grasp on housing needs and potential barriers to maintaining stable housing.
* Experience managing crisis situations, skilled at crisis response, crisis de\-escalation, and risk mitigation.
* Passionate about working with adults who may be isolated, have mental health issues, have cognitive impairments, substance abuse issues, or other needs that are not being met.
* Demonstrated outreach, rapport building, and engagement experience.
* Ability to travel in SF and work in office, community, home, and hospital settings.
* Strong skills in working independently and also as a team member.
* Strong organizational, communication, interpersonal, and time management skills and ability to prioritize projects and follow through.
